text:
Marathon Petroleum stock surged 2.6% today, extending a roughly 8% rally over two weeks. The move follows major news on oil supply tightness: Saudi Aramco's CEO warned that rebuilding global oil stockpiles could take up to two years, while the U.S.-Iran conflict continues to disrupt Middle Eastern production and shipping. With U.S. refineries running at 92.5% capacity and crude prices climbing—domestic oil at $96/barrel and global crude at nearly $114/barrel—refiners like Marathon stand to capture wider profit margins on fuel sales as supplies remain constrained.

The broader backdrop amplifies this: the G7's plan to release 100 million barrels from reserves over four months is a drop against the structural supply squeeze. Rising geopolitical tensions, diesel shortages across Europe and the U.S., and the multi-year timeline to restore inventory all point to sustained high fuel prices and strong margins for refiners over the near term.
